leading_positions.synthesis: Four of the eight round-1 configurations prefer optical lattice clocks with Katori and Ye as a two-name prize. Shared: the magic-wavelength idea plus the 10^-18 realisation, reproduction by several independent laboratories, and the view that it differs from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-clock recognitions. Not shared: how to weigh Katori's concept against the performance records of Ye's group, and how far the citation should name concept and realisation rather than the precision record. Johansson and Pearce moved to B006 from other first choices after reading the openings (circuit QED and IceCube respectively). Their alternatives differ: B004 and B012 for Kroll, B004 and B043 for Pearce, B004 and B023 for Johansson, B023 and B004 for Lindroth. Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson, who prefer other ballots, list B006 as an alternative.

Two members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene with MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero. Shared: a compact Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction followed by the 2018 experimental discovery, reproduction across many groups, and a new tunable platform for correlated matter. Not shared in detail: both hold B004 as an alternative, but Mehlig adds B023 while Olsson adds B006. Both concede that the unresolved superconducting mechanism, the omitted first author of the 2018 experiments and the age of the field (about eight years) are real weaknesses, and both would keep Bistritzer in the trio.

One member prefers topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. The case rests on a new symmetry-protected state of matter, a decisive HgTe experiment and nearly two decades of independent confirmation. The same member accepts that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, the three-dimensional work and the 2016 topological-phases prize leave an untidy credit boundary. B004 is named as an alternative in seven files (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce); only Eriksson prefers it.

One member prefers IceCube and neutrino astronomy with Halzen and Spiering, resting the citation on the independently seen astrophysical flux rather than on source identification. That member holds the position with less certainty than in the opening, mainly because of attribution (Baikal, AMANDA, DUMAND precursors; a collaboration of hundreds). Pearce, who opened with B043 first, now lists it only as an alternative. Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce each point to the modest single-source significance of TXS 0506+056.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's preferred configuration is a single-part prize of two or three names; no member proposes a multi-part prize in round 1.
B006, B004 and B009 are named by several members as either preferred configurations or alternatives, so the practical contest in round 1 is among these three, with B043 held by one member.

Members who rank B006 judge its reproducibility and maturity to be strong and its two-name credit to be comparatively clean; even those who prefer other ballots (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson) describe it as mature or a safe alternative.
Several members state that a citation should be worded around observed phenomena or the named invention and its realisation, not around an unresolved mechanism or a general precision record.
Members state that their views rely on memory of the literature and that outside expert reports are needed to settle priority questions.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks (B006) count as a new invention and discovery in the sense the prize requires, or as a precision advance following the 2005 frequency-comb prize and 2012 ion-clock prize. Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce argue it is a distinct invention; the overlap objection is raised in their own files and by Danielsson (who has since softened), and Eriksson asks whether a new state of matter should take priority over a better ruler.

Whether the Z2 topological-insulator step (B004) is sufficiently distinct from the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and topological phases of matter. Eriksson argues it is a separate symmetry-protected class; Mehlig, Olsson and Danielsson raise the overlap.

Whether the IceCube result (B043) can be cited for more than the diffuse flux, given that the TXS 0506+056 association is a single-source result of modest significance and the Galactic-plane map is diffuse.
attribution_disputes: B006: whether Ludlow, Lemonde, Hinkley, Bloom and the Yb, Hg, Al+ and ion-clock communities, or the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups, have claims that a Katori-Ye pair leaves out, and how to weigh Katori's magic-wavelength priority against Ye's record performance. Several members have not checked the 2001-03 priority record.

B009: whether Bistritzer should stay beside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and how to treat first author Yuan Cao and other 2018 experimentalists, as well as earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell; Kaxiras, Santos).

B004: whether Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang deceased in 2018), or Fu and Moore and Balents and Hasan for the three-dimensional phase, should be credited alongside or instead of one of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp.
B043: whether Spiering, or another early leader of AMANDA, Baikal or DUMAND, should stand beside Halzen, and how a two-name award relates to a collaboration of hundreds.

B023 and B015 are raised in discussion without a preferred supporter: B023 has five credited names and members' trios differ (Bloch, Cirac, Zoller versus Bloch, Greiner, Zoller); B015 omits Wallraff from a three-name prize.
maturity_disputes: B009: the superconducting pairing mechanism is open and the field is about eight years old. Mehlig and Olsson accept this but argue the phenomena are reproduced; Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Pearce and Danielsson regard it as a maturity concern.

B043: members who rank it lower (Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) say the astrophysical interpretation and source identification are still developing; Danielsson answers that the flux has been independently confirmed and the tradition does not wait for every question to be answered.

B006: the redefinition of the SI second has not happened and fundamental-physics payoffs (varying constants, dark matter) are still pending; members differ on whether this counts for or against timing.
B015: timing is questioned because the 2025 prize recognised superconducting circuits (Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Chalmers, director of WACQT) discloses a possible recusal issue on B015, circuit QED, through close ties to the Yale and ETH-linked community around Schoelkopf, Girvin, Blais and Wallraff and to Chalmers colleagues; B015 is no longer in Johansson's configuration.
Olsson (transmission electron microscopist) says B012, aberration correction, is in her own field and she would step back from or treat that ballot with caution.

Kroll discloses a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during his PhD (Hall's JILA environment is Ye's institution) and work in atomic physics at Lund; he reports no collaboration with Katori or Ye and defers to the committee on recusal for B006.

Lindroth discloses close collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and work in atomic, molecular and optical physics near the clock and cold-atom candidates; she does not see this as a reason to recuse.
Pearce (chair) works in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, not IceCube, and notes possible proximity bias toward B043.
Mehlig notes only a shared Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson. Danielsson and Eriksson report no specific conflicts.
questions_for_round2: Does the committee accept the optical lattice clock (B006) as a new invention distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-clock prizes, and can members who see it as incremental say what additional evidence would change that view?

Should a B006 citation name the magic-wavelength concept and its realisation at 10^-18, and is a Katori-Ye pair defensible given the claims of Ludlow, Lemonde, Hinkley and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups? Is an expert report on 2001-03 priority needed?

Mehlig and Olsson prefer B009 and Eriksson prefers B004. Can those three, together with others who rank these ballots, state what they would accept as a settled credit boundary (Bistritzer, Yuan Cao, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) and whether maturity or attribution is the decisive obstacle in each case?
Is B004 close enough to the 2016 topological-phases prize that the committee would be repeating a subject, or is the Z2 symmetry-protected class a separate step?

Can the B043 citation rest on the detection of the diffuse astrophysical flux alone, and what would Danielsson and Pearce need from an outside report on Halzen, Spiering and the AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND precursors to keep it as a live alternative?
Does the committee want a single two-name part, or could a second distinct part be added without exceeding three laureates, and which ballot would be the candidate?
Do the disclosures by Kroll and Lindroth (links to JILA-adjacent and AMO environments) and by Johansson and Olsson require recusal or limited participation on any ballot, and who rules on that?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a plurality for B006 (four of eight explicit first preferences), two for B009, and one each for B004 and B043. The lead is built on a move by two members after reading openings and rests on shared reproducibility and credit-clarity arguments, while the main stated objection (overlap with the comb and ion-clock prizes) and the priority question have not been tested against expert reports. The B009, B004 and B043 positions are each held mainly on scientific novelty and each faces an attribution or maturity objection from its own supporters. No vote is implied beyond the positions stated in the eight files.
